findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading (Senate floor, 6:13 PM); Craven voted Aye; the Senate vote was 28 Aye, 13 No, 9 not voting, passed
findings.note: Voted for HB 958 on second reading in the Senate. The ratified bill (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf) says a voter registration application, including one made at a drivers license office, is processed only if the applicant affirmatively states US citizenship; a blank answer gets a notice and a 30-day window to return a citizenship statement under penalty of perjury. It also directs the State Board of Elections to create a process to remove voters flagged as possible non-citizens from a federal database, and to remove deceased voters from the rolls weekly. It has no photo ID provision that I found. The bill page shows 'Vetoed 08/17/2026'. His vote page (https://www.ncleg.gov/Members/Votes/S/423) lists no third-reading or override vote on HB 958.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Amendment 1 adopted (5:06 PM) and Amendment 5 adopted (5:28 PM); motions to table Amendments 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 (5:11 to 6:04 PM) passed; Craven voted Aye on each
findings.note: His votes page shows Aye on each of these floor votes on HB 958 on 7/28/2026. The page does not give the text of the amendments, and I did not read them, so what each one does is not stated here.

findings.motion: Senate second reading, H 958 Election Law Changes (28-13)
findings.note: Listed among the Ayes on the Senate second-reading vote on H 958, the election law changes bill. The ratified bill (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf) requires a registration application to state that the applicant is a U.S. citizen before it is processed, with a 30-day sworn-statement fix if the answer is blank, and sets up a process to remove voters flagged as possible non-citizens by a federal database. The bill page shows a Governor's veto on 2026-08-17.
